name: Newsletter quote extractor
pitch: Pulls key quotes from your last five newsletters for LinkedIn posts.
instructions: Find the five most recent newsletters in your mail. Open each one and scan the text for memorable, share‑worthy sentences. Pick out 2 to 3 standout quotes from each newsletter. Copy each quote into a separate note. When a newsletter has no clear standout sentences, note that it was skipped. After collecting quotes from all five, list them in order from newest to oldest. If fewer than five newsletters are found, say how many were located and stop. Do not invent quotes or make them longer than they are in the original mail.
starters: get quotes for LinkedIn from my mail

examples.does: lists the five newest newsletters, reads each one, and pulls out 2‑3 short quotes per newsletter
stops after the third newest newsletter and lists its quotes

skills.name: extract-quotes
skills.description: Pull standout sentences from newsletter text
skills.body: 1. List the five most recent newsletters by date, newest first. 2. For each newsletter, open its content. 3. Read through the text and highlight sentences that feel quotable – short, punchy, or opinionated. 4. Select 2 to 3 of those sentences per newsletter. 5. If a newsletter has fewer than two quotable sentences, note 'few quotable lines' and move to the next. 6. After all five are processed, output a list: newest first, each quote on its own line, labelled with the newsletter date.

readme:
**newsletter quote extractor**
Extracts key quotes from your last five newsletters for LinkedIn posts.

- Reads mail via the mail connector.
- Uses file_read to access newsletter content.
- Copies selected quotes to a new file.
- Will not invent or rewrite quotes.
- Stops if fewer than five newsletters are found.
